wave_type: Rayleigh surface wave on a free plane surface
geometry: Homogeneous isotropic elastic solid bounded by the plane z = 0; disturbance confined to a superficial stratum whose thickness is comparable with the wavelength (printed p.4).
boundary_or_interface_conditions: Tangential stress components vanish at z = 0 (eq (20)); normal traction zero at the surface (eq (22)); solution chosen with the exponent that decays into the solid (p.5).
secular_equation_ref: Eq (23) printed p.6: {2(f^2+g^2) - h^2}^2 = 4 r s (f^2+g^2); rationalised to eq (24), a polynomial in k^2 of degree 4 (OCR of exponents uncertain). Variables: f, g = wavenumbers along x and y; h^2 = rho p^2/(lambda+2mu); k^2 = rho p^2/mu; r^2 = f^2+g^2-h^2; s^2 = f^2+g^2-k^2.
existence_condition: No existence criterion stated for the general case. For the incompressible solid (lambda = infinity, h^2 = 0) eq (25) k^6 - 8k^4 + 24k^2 - 16 = 0 has the real root k^2 = .91275 (f^2+g^2) (p.8).
limiting_cases: Incompressible limit: eq (25), k^2 = .91275 (f^2+g^2), k = .9554 f, s = .2954 f (pp.8-9). Finite compressibility: the paper tabulates h^2/(f^2+g^2) and k/sqrt(f^2+g^2) against lambda/mu (Poisson ratio) (p.10).
physical_mode_statement: Complex roots of the squared equation are rejected: for k^2 = 3.5436 +- 2.2301i the real part of s has the opposite sign to r, so that exp(rz) and exp(-sz) do not both vanish with depth; the complex values are dismissed and only k^2 = .91275 (f^2+g^2) is kept (pp.8-9).
numerical_examples_printed: Incompressible solid: speed .9554 sqrt(mu/rho) (p.9); k = .9554f, s = .2954f (eq (32), p.8); horizontal motion vanishes at z = .8659, i.e. .1378 lambda' below the surface (p.9); surface amplitudes a = .4567, gamma = -.840 (eq (34), p.9). Compressible example (second table case) r^2 = -.7182, s^2 = -.1547(f^2+g^2), s = .3933 sqrt(f^2+g^2), h^2 gamma/f = -.6204 (eqs (37)-(39), pp.10-11); table values .9127 .8453 .7640 .4746 and .9554 .9194 .8741 .6896 (p.10).
notes: Read from the page text layer of f.pdf (pp.4-11 of Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. 17). Old-scan OCR renders superscripts inconsistently (h2, k*, lci); equations reproduced here in words or in plain ASCII with the mark 'OCR uncertain' where the exponent or exponent sign is doubtful. Table column headings on p.10 were not recoverable from the text layer.

wave_type: Transverse (Love) waves in a superficial layer; Rayleigh-type waves over a layered half-space
geometry: Layer of thickness T (0 <= z <= T) resting on a half-space (z < 0), origin on the lower boundary, z upwards; layer rigidity and density mu, rho; substratum mu', rho' (printed p.161).
boundary_or_interface_conditions: At z = 0 displacement and tangential traction continuous: A = C and mu s B = mu' s' C. Upper boundary z = T free of traction: -mu s A sin(sT) + mu s B cos(sT) = 0 (p.161).
secular_equation_ref: Eq (40) printed p.162: tan(sT) = mu' s'/(mu s), with s^2 = p^2 p/ mu - f^2 (35), s'^2 = f^2 - p^2 p/mu' (39). Used with (41) and (43) to connect s and f; variables: f wavenumber, p frequency, T thickness.
existence_condition: 'The condition of reality cannot be satisfied unless b' > b' (p.162), where b and b' are the distortional wave speeds; restated in section 181 (p.164): transverse waves cannot be transmitted through the layer without penetrating far into the substratum unless b' > b.
limiting_cases: As f tends to 0 the wave velocity tends to b'; as s tends to pi/2, so that f tends to infinity, the velocity tends to b (p.163). Wave velocity increases with wavelength. Types with one or more horizontal nodal planes inside the layer (p.163) and a second type of superficial waves (pp.173-174, eq (69)).
physical_mode_statement: Decay of the substratum disturbance requires s' > 0 (p.161); the amplitude falls by the ratio exp(-s'T) in one layer thickness, and the waves are practically confined to the layer when s'T is large (p.162). Waves of the second type penetrate more freely into the interior (p.163).
numerical_examples_printed: Section 187, p.171: with fT = 6, s/f = .25 and rho' = rho the wave velocity is (.9682) b against (.9553) b for simple Rayleigh waves; the positive root W is about 2.65, giving mu'/mu = 2.325 (rigidity of the lower medium a little more than twice that of the layer) and a velocity about 1 per cent above the Rayleigh value. Section 188, p.173: vertical to horizontal amplitude ratio about 2, as Rayleigh found. p.160: rigidity 2.5e11 dyn/cm^2 and density 2.8 give a Rayleigh velocity of about 3 km/s by the formula '0.9 sqrt(mu/rho)'.
notes: Book scan from the Internet Archive (someproblemsofge00loveuoft.pdf, 218 pages); chapter XI, sections 176-188, printed pp.160-174. Running page numbers are printed in the text and were used to fix the page. AI reading of plain text only.

wave_type: Interfacial (Stoneley) wave between two bonded elastic half-spaces
geometry: Two semi-infinite isotropic elastic media welded at the plane z = 0; axis z drawn into medium 1; wave propagated in the x direction; displacement of the form (U,V,W) exp ik(x - ct) with U,V,W functions of z alone (p.417).
boundary_or_interface_conditions: Displacements and stresses continuous at z = 0 (eqs (11)-(16), pp.417-418); solutions chosen to vanish at infinite distance from z = 0: r1^2, s1^2, r2^2, s2^2 given by (4),(5),(9),(10) (p.417).
secular_equation_ref: Eq (23), printed p.418: a 4 x 4 determinant of the four interface equations (19)-(22) set equal to zero, entries built from rho1, rho2, mu1, mu2, beta1^2 = mu1/rho1, beta2^2 = mu2/rho2, alpha1^2 = (lambda1+2mu1)/rho1, alpha2^2, and the wave velocity c. Reduced in section 3 to the quartic (1) of p.419 with A1, A2, B1, B2 and K = 2(rho1 beta1^2 - rho2 beta2^2).
existence_condition: 'It is essential that c should be positive and less than both beta1 and beta2' (pp.422-423). For alpha1 = alpha2, beta1 = beta2 a root always exists between x = 0 and x = 1 (p.420). Existence is not general: 'not if the wave-velocities are greatly different' (p.423).
limiting_cases: rho2 = 0 reduces (1) to the Rayleigh equation (2) (p.419). rho1 = rho2 gives x = 1 or 1/gamma, i.e. c = beta or c = alpha (p.420). Incompressible media treated separately in section 4, eq (1) with coefficients A-D (p.421).
physical_mode_statement: Complex roots are rejected because the disturbances 'will not both be real, and ... will not be insensible at great distance from the surface of separation' (p.423); explicitly, for c^2/beta^2 = .75806 +- 1.57720i the ratio s/kappa has a negative real part in the numerator, so exp(-sz) and exp(-kappa z) cannot both tend to zero (p.422). Squaring in the reduction to (8) also produced roots that satisfy the squared but not the original equation and are discarded (p.423).
numerical_examples_printed: p.422: rho1 = 8.2, rho2 = 3.2 (Wiechert density law) give 16889.6(c/beta)^6 - 4225.6(c/beta)^4 + 77796.0(c/beta)^2 - 51984.0 = 0 with root c = .99287 beta, i.e. a velocity very slightly less than the distortional speed in either medium; the complex root c^2/beta^2 = .75806 +- 1.57720i is printed and rejected. p.423: rho1 = 2 rho2 with beta2^2 = 2 beta1^2 gives 81(c/beta1)^4 - 432(c/beta1)^2 + 640 = 0, no real roots; rho1 = 2, rho2 = 1, beta1^2 = 2 beta2^2 gives eq (10) with no root between y = 0 and y = 1; rho1 = 2, rho2 = 1, beta2^2 = (2/3) beta1^2 gives eq (11) with x^2 = .9042 and .93615, both extraneous.
notes: c.pdf is an image-only scan (no text layer). Read page by page from rendered page images at 160 dpi, pp.416-428. Equations (23) and (19)-(22) are long determinants and were described, not retyped. The journal is Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 106 (1924) 416-428; DOI is printed on the cover page.

wave_type: Stoneley waves between two media; generalized Rayleigh waves in a superficial layer
geometry: Two half-spaces for the Stoneley problem; a layer of thickness T over a half-space for the general problem, with T/L as the parameter (L = transverse wavelength in the layer) (p.120).
boundary_or_interface_conditions: Not restated; the paper refers to its 1942 papers for the derivation. The boundary curves are obtained from the Stoneley equation and from the period equation of an isolated layer (Lamb, Proc. Roy. Soc. A 93, 114, 1917) (p.123).
secular_equation_ref: Stoneley boundary curves, eqs (1) and (2) (pp.120-121), in rho/rho', w = (beta'/beta)^2, v = mu/(lambda+2mu), v' = mu'/(lambda'+2mu'); layer period equation (3) (p.123); limiting form (4) (p.125); exact boundary curves of the one- and two-SWS regions (p.126).
existence_condition: Stoneley waves 'can exist for every value of rho/rho', mu/mu' which lies between the two curves' (p.120). For the layer: 'there exists a surface wave system (SWS) for every value of rho/rho' and T/L if beta > S', S being the Rayleigh velocity of the layer material; if beta < S only for small enough rho/rho' and small T/L (p.122).
limiting_cases: The two limits T/L -> 0 (Bromwich, thin layer) and T/L -> infinity (Love, Stoneley) are distinguished at the outset (p.120); the period equation splits into the Rayleigh equation of the upper medium and the Stoneley equation as T/L tends to infinity. Asymptote of curve A: rho/rho' = 2.9117 when lambda/rho = lambda'/rho', 3.2360 when lambda = lambda' = infinity (p.122); limiting root of (2) 2.91 and 3.27 respectively (p.125); root of (4) about 1 (lambda/rho = lambda'/rho') and 1.12 (lambda = lambda' = infinity) (p.125).
physical_mode_statement: Existence is stated region by region: 'in the horizontally shaded area no SWS can exist' (p.124); two SWS possible in the vertically shaded area (p.124). No decay or radiation criterion is derived here; existence only.
numerical_examples_printed: p.124: for beta' = 1.413 the solution of (2) reads rho/rho' = 2 and the root of (3) reads T/L = 4.4, so a SWS exists for every rho/rho' and T/L; the second example (beta of order 1.4 beta') gives rho/rho' = .5 and T/L = .4, so a SWS exists for every T/L if rho/rho' < .5 and for every rho/rho' if T/L < .4. These are readings from Figs. 3 and 4, printed as such. p.122: asymptote values 2.9117 and 3.2360.
notes: d.pdf has a poor text layer: Greek letters are mangled (rho printed as p, beta as /3, lambda as A) and equations (1)-(3) are partly illegible. Numeric values above are those the text layer shows clearly; equations are described rather than reconstructed. Journal: Geophys. Suppl. (M. N. R. A. S.) 5, 120-126, received 1946 April 23; no DOI printed.

wave_type: Interfacial (Stoneley) waves in bonded anisotropic elastic half-spaces
geometry: Two bonded linear elastic half-spaces of arbitrary anisotropy, interface n.x = 0, n the unit normal, m the wave normal in the interface, t = m x n (p.154, Fig. 1 p.155).
boundary_or_interface_conditions: Continuity of displacements (2.5)-(2.6) and of tractions (2.7) at the interface, the latter written with the half-space surface impedance tensors Z(1), Z(2); partial waves decaying away from the interface, Im p_alpha(1) > 0 and Im p_alpha*(2) < 0 (p.155).
secular_equation_ref: Existence equation (2.11) det A = 0 at v = v_s, where A = Z(1) + Z^T(2) is the 3 x 3 hermitian interface impedance matrix (2.8)-(2.10), p.156; equivalently the vanishing of the determinant of a 3 x 3 skew hermitian matrix as stated on p.154.
existence_condition: Subsonic interval (2.3)-(2.4): 0 <= v <= v_hat(1) <= v_hat(2); 'a subsonic Stoneley wave solution exists if and only if there exists a speed v_s, 0 < v_s < v_hat(1), such that (2.8) is satisfied, which in turn requires that det A = 0' (p.156). Uniqueness: 'either one or no subsonic Stoneley mode exists' (p.154).
limiting_cases: The isotropic case is related to Scholte (1942) and Cagniard (1962) on p.154; the Stoneley speed is stated to exceed the slower of the Rayleigh speeds of the separate half-spaces whenever a Stoneley wave exists (p.154).
physical_mode_statement: Only subsonic speeds with exponentially decaying partial waves are admitted (2.3), p.155; uniqueness of the subsonic mode is proved in the paper (p.154). No root-counting without the decay test.
numerical_examples_printed: None printed by the authors in the pages read. The copper bi-crystal numerical search quoted on p.154 is Tholen (1984), cited, not the authors' own computation.
notes: e.pdf is an image-only scan (no text layer); read from rendered page images, pp.153-156. Sections 3-5 (theorems and the numerical criterion implementation) were not transcribed, so only the formulation and the existence equations (2.3)-(2.11) are recorded. Journal: Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 402 (1985) 153-166; DOI printed on the cover page.

geometry: Functionally graded piezoelectric half-space x2 > 0 (hexagonal 6 mm), free surface x2 = 0; c44, e15, epsilon11 and rho all proportional to one inhomogeneity function f(x2) (p.695).
boundary_or_interface_conditions: Metalized surface: phi(0) = 0 and t23(0) = 0. Free surface: t23(0) = 0 and d2(0) = ik epsilon0 phi(0) (pp.699-700). Decay with depth required through Re(q) > 0 in (3.7).
secular_equation_ref: Metalized (3.15) and free (3.17) dispersion equations for profiles P0-P5, p.699-700; metalized (3.20) and free (3.21) for profiles P6-P10, p.700; homogeneous limits (3.16) and (3.18). Variables: v speed, v_T bulk shear speed, chi^2 = e15^2/(c44 epsilon11 + e15^2), f'(0), c0 and k from the profile.
existence_condition: Subsonic interval (3.12): 0 < (v/v_T)^2 < 1 + c0/k^2, p.699; for the trigonometric profiles this gives beta^2 < k^2. For the exponential example the admissible range is beta/k < chi^2/(2 sqrt(1+chi^2)) = 0.2015 (p.701); for the inverse-quadratic example the decay condition reduces to v < v_T (p.701).
limiting_cases: f identically 1 recovers the homogeneous Bleustein-Gulyaev wave, non-dispersive, with (v_m/v_T)^2 = 1 - chi^4 (3.16) and (v_f/v_T)^2 = 1 - chi^4/(1+epsilon11/epsilon0)^2 (3.18); beta/k -> 0 recovers the homogeneous speeds in Fig. 1 (p.701).
physical_mode_statement: Attenuation factors (3.11) must have positive real part; the paper notes that (3.12) ensures u_hat(infinity) = 0 'but, because u = (1/sqrt f) u_hat, not necessarily that u(infinity) = 0; this latter condition must be tested a posteriori against each different form of f' (p.699).
numerical_examples_printed: PZT-4 interface constants c44 = 2.56e10 N/m^2, e15 = 12.7 C/m^2, epsilon11 = 650e-11 F/m, rho = 7500 kg/m^3, epsilon0 = 8.854e-12 F/m (p.700); homogeneous speeds v_m = 2256.85 m/s and v_f = 2592.65 m/s, K2S about 0.242 (p.701); exponential profile with beta/k from 0 to 0.2 raises K2S from 0.242 to 0.324 (Fig. 1(b), p.701).
